When your queue ends, keep similar music playing.
Turns hi-res output off while on.
AAC uses about a fifth of the data and starts faster. Applies from the next song.
Songs mixed in Dolby Atmos play that mix (E-AC-3, about 768 kbps), decoded by the phone\'s Dolby decoder when it has one. Other songs keep the quality above. Applies from the next song.
Songs mixed in Dolby Atmos play a headphone render of that mix (AAC 256 kbps), spatial on any headphones. Other songs keep the quality above. Applies from the next song.
Songs always play in the quality above, even when they have a Dolby Atmos mix.
Off while Skip silence is on: trimming silence needs 16-bit processing.
Decode to 32-bit float so 24-bit audio is not reduced to 16-bit. Applies the next time playback starts.

For USB DACs only: each song plays at its own rate and bit depth, untouched by the system. While a USB DAC is connected the DAC controls the volume, and the equalizer and the other effects are off. Stereo only: Dolby Atmos plays through the system as usual, effects included. Applies from the next song.
How much of the upcoming song is downloaded and decrypted ahead of time, so it starts without a gap.
Lets “back” start at once instead of loading.
Whole songs of the queue downloaded and decrypted around the one playing, so skipping either way is instant.
Off keeps those songs for Wi-Fi; the preload above always works.
The most decrypted audio kept on this device; the songs ahead and behind never go past it. The song that is playing is always downloaded in full.
Sweep each word as it\'s sung, when timing is available.
Soften lines further from the one being sung.
Remember what you play for History and Recently Played.
A Material 3 Expressive player with an in-process lossless downloader.
Each segment is fetched, decrypted and muxed as it arrives (the same path playback uses) instead of downloading the whole file and then decrypting it.
Download straight from what playback already decrypted, so a track you just played saves almost instantly. Off keeps a separate download cache.
Folder and file templates use tokens like {artist}, {album}, {year}, {track:02d} and {title}. A custom folder keeps the decrypted masters there; otherwise they are published to Music/Cadence.
Where albums, playlists and singles go unless a type overrides it.
Pick a folder with the system picker. The folder name is fixed; sub-folders still come from the naming template.
Previews use \"Daft Punk — Random Access Memories\", track 7 \"Touch\", 2013-05-17.
Tokens are replaced at download time.
Songs mixed in Dolby Atmos are saved as that mix (E-AC-3, about 768 kbps, in an .m4a). It needs a player with a Dolby decoder; other songs keep the format above.
Songs mixed in Dolby Atmos are saved as their headphone render (AAC 256 kbps), spatial on any headphones and any player. Other songs keep the format above.
Songs are always saved in the format above, even when they have a Dolby Atmos mix.
Title, artist, album, track, disc, date and genre into the file.
Even out the volume between songs, applied to every output.
used until a song\'s loudness has been measured
A limiter keeps any boost (replay gain, equalizer, tone) from clipping, without the distortion of a hard clip.

Apple\'s stream ships no loudness data, so Cadence measures each song (EBU R128) the first time it plays through and levels it to -18 LUFS from then on. Until a song is measured, the \"info missing\" preamp applies. Album mode uses the album\'s measured songs.
Pan and stereo width, applied to every output, hi-res included. Stereo only.
Width is mid/side: 0 is mono, 1 is the original stereo, 2 widens it. Balance keeps the side you turn toward at full level and lowers the other.
Bass and treble shelves, applied to every output, hi-res included.
Gains are in dB (±%1$s). Tone shelves run before the equalizer.
A 10-band equalizer applied to every output, hi-res included.
Lowers the level by the curve\'s largest boost, so boosting never clips. A limiter still catches what is left.

Loads an AutoEQ profile: the ParametricEQ.txt file for your headphone model, from autoeq.app or the AutoEq repository. It runs before the bands, so they stay free for your taste. With auto headroom on, the level drops by the profile\'s largest boost; with it off, the file\'s preamp applies.
No filters found. Load the ParametricEQ.txt file from AutoEQ.
A filter is out of range: %1$s
The file could not be read.
Gains are in dB (±%1$s). If boosts distort, lower the preamp to make room.
Smooth 16-bit quantization. Only active on a 16-bit output.
Triangular (TPDF) is the safe default: it decouples both the level and the loudness of the noise from the music. Noise-shaped pushes that noise up where the ear is least sensitive.
One uniform noise step. Decorrelates error.
Two-step triangular noise. The standard choice.
Triangular plus noise shaping toward high frequencies.
Bit-for-bit identical to the studio master, sampled above CD and streaming rates.
Bit-for-bit identical to the original recording. Nothing is thrown away.
Spatial audio mix (Dolby Atmos / E-AC-3) downmixed or rendered for stereo headphones.
Compressed to save space. Some detail is discarded, usually inaudibly.
